title: Bid counts: null is not zero, and received is not solicited
why: Three phrasings appear in this one document. Only one of them states both numbers. Writing 0 for 'not stated', or copying the received count into the solicited count, turns a missing value into a false competitive signal -- 'one bid solicited, one received' means sole-source, and inventing it is the opposite of a truthful extraction.
verified_against: the announcement prose, by hand. Not verified against any model output -- cache/llm/ is empty.

select.contractor_raw: South Carolina Commission for the Blind

checks.quote: One bid was solicited with one received.
checks.reason: Both counts are stated in words. 1 / 1.

checks.quote: Bids were solicited via the internet with one received.
checks.reason: 'via the internet' is a method, not a count. bids_solicited must stay null; bids_received is 1.

checks.quote: Bids were solicited via the internet with 19 received.
checks.reason: Same phrasing with a large received count. 19 must not be copied into bids_solicited.

checks.quote: This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with four offers received. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Mid-Atlantic, Norfolk, Virginia, is the contracting activity (N40085-26-C-0020).
checks.reason: 'four offers received' spelled out -> bids_received 4, bids_solicited null.

checks.quote: Bids were solicited via the internet with 19 received.
checks.reason: No entry in this document states that zero bids were solicited. A 0 anywhere in this column means 'not stated' was written as zero.

checks.quote: This award is the result of a sole-source acquisition.
checks.reason: Several entries state no bid counts at all (the Northrop Grumman sole-source task order among them). Those must be null / null, not 0 / 0.
